messages:
sam: Starting thread for the cross-service release queue (API/runtime/console/router). Deploybot scheduled wave-2 at 02:00 UTC. Need quick thumbs on two items: a) runtime kernel bump (1.12->1.13) compatibility b) console migration ordering.

deploy-bot: Deploy wave scheduled. Wave id: wave-2026-02-02-B. Current blockers: console-migration v3 not applied in staging; runtime kernel image tagged 'canary-1.13' pending approval. See /deploy wave details: https://deploy.internal/wave-2026-02-02-B

sam: @taylor can you confirm runtime kernel bump is clean for the model-serving path? We need KV cache behavior validated (esp eviction).

taylor: Quick check: kernel bump passes unit + integration on lightweight traces but we saw one flaky test on KV eviction under burst. Investigating now. Expect update in ~20m.

maria: Console migration v3 modifies the saved-route schema. If we apply console first, router will reject old header split format. We need to pin router to accept both schemas for a short window.

cj: Router team can add a tolerant header-parser flag, but it requires a small config rollout. I can flip the flag in prod canary and watch for 5m.

sam: Proposal: hold canary to 10% until kernel bump + tolerant header flag are green. If either fails, rollback path is: revert console migration and abort wave. Agree?

taylor: I can get kernel stress run in ~15m. If eviction repros, we should consider a temporary cache-size limit as a mitigation (config), not full rollback.

maria: Noted. Console migration also has DB migration that is backwards-compatible if we add router tolerate flag. So rollback is pretty safe but a little messy.

cj: Starting flag flip in canary: //router:configs/accept-legacy-header = true

deploy-bot: Flag flip executed in canary (canary-3). Monitoring 10m.

sre-bot: Canary metrics snapshot at t+5m: 200 RPS, error-rate spike +0.6% (within noise), p95 latency +12ms. No backend errors observed.

sam: Good. @taylor status on runtime stress?

taylor: Stress run completed. KV eviction spike reproduced on a synthetic workload that hits 3x token-length. Root cause: LRU eviction interacts with continuous batching kernel path after bump. I have a fix branch that avoids aggressive eviction during warmup.

sam: Two options: a) merge backport hotfix to runtime and re-run canary (adds ~30-40m), b) apply cache-size cap config to reduce eviction pressure and proceed. Which gives better risk profile?

taylor: Hotfix is safer long-term but takes time. Config cap is low-risk and reversible. I'd go config cap for this wave.

maria: Agree. Config cap + router tolerate flag keeps console migration safe. We should note in release notes: "temporary runtime cache cap enabled due to eviction under high seq workloads — will be removed after hotfix."

sam: OK doing config cap. cj, hold console migration start until I confirm.

cj: Holding. Also adding short rollback playbook to the wave notes.

deploy-bot: Applying runtime config: runtime.cache.max_entries=120000 in prod canary. Change id: cfg-8702.

sre-bot: Post-config metrics: no eviction spikes in synthetic run, p95 steady. Rolling to 10% traffic.

sam: All right. We're green to proceed with canary 10% and console migration start. Reminder: tagging release notes with the mitigation and follow-up hotfix ticket (INF-3421).

maria: Noted. I'll publish migration plan and the contingency steps in the wave doc.

cj: Console migration started in canary. Watching router logs for header parsing warnings.

sre-bot: Router canary logs: <5 warnings related to legacy headers, no rejects.

sam: If anything above 1% rejects or errors, immediate abort and revert console migration. Everyone ok with that guardrail?

all: :thumbsup:

sam: Final checklist before wave rollout: 1) runtime config cap in place (done) 2) router tolerate flag (done) 3) console migration canary applied (done) 4) deploybot wave ramp plan (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m) 5) rollback owner assigned: @maria for console, @taylor for runtime, @cj for router.

deploy-bot: Wave ramping: 10% -> 50% in 10m if metrics stable. Auto-rollback thresholds: error-rate >=1% OR p95 increase >=150ms sustained 5m.

sam: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread for the live rollout notes. If we hit auto-rollback, declare reason and next steps here.

maria: Adding runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/console-migration-wave-2026-B

cj: Tagging follow-up: open ticket INF-3421-hotfix-runtime-eviction (to track hotfix + revert of config cap).

sre-bot: Wave scaled to 50% at t+18m. Metrics stable.

sam: Good job. Post-rollout: please add a 1-paragraph note to release notes with mitigation + owners. We'll remove the runtime cap on hotfix merge.

maria: Will do.

cj: Noted.

deploy-bot: Wave completed to 100% at t+35m. No auto-rollback triggered.

sam: Closing thread — leaving notes and retitle wave for postmortem later. Thanks everyone.
